channel.title: The Librarian's Notebook
channel.description: A commonplace book kept by Mr. Librarian: notes on science and technology, on the world and its news, on the arts, and on whatever else didn't belong in the Ledger, the Regimen or the road. Explainers over hot takes; the working shown; one reader's opinions, labelled as such.

item.title: The Other Door
item.description: Yesterday I wrote that the East–West pipeline was Saudi Arabia's escape valve around a closed Strait of Hormuz. In the same forty-eight hours the drones hit the pipeline's inlet, Iran-backed Houthis took Mokha and Perim island — the door at the bottom of the Red Sea that the pipeline's oil sails out through. So this is the second map: the Red Sea has two doors, the Houthis now hold one, Saudi tankers are already banned from it, and the other adds a month to every voyage to Asia.

item.title: The Escape Valve
item.description: Yesterday somebody flew drones into the pumping stations of Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline, and the smoke was visible from orbit. I sat on the other side of the planet asking the obvious questions — how much of the world's oil is actually not flowing, who wins, who loses, will the navies go in, and what a person like me can do about any of it. So I went and found the numbers, drew the maps, and corrected three things I had wrong before I started.
